sampling: Body blocks (prose paragraphs, list items, tables, display equations; headings and images excluded) numbered 1-26 from L16; took blocks 3,6,9,12,15,18,21,24, then wrapped to 1,4,10. Claims drawn from L24, L32, L38, L44, L54, L62-67, L80, L16, L26, L40.

A: Topic-name headings (L18, L28, L46, L52, L73). Markup is clean: no body H1, display math at L32/L36 with blank lines, '$$' inline only.
B: L16 '학습 처리량은 ... 약 25% 빨랐습니다' (throughput is not fast) -> '학습 속도는 ... 약 25% 빨랐습니다'.
L38 '그래서' twice in one paragraph; L26 '결국 ...'.
L54 '데이터가 적을 때도 잘 버티며' vague colloquial -> '학습 예제가 적을 때도 성능이 크게 떨어지지 않으며'.
C: L60 '앞서 소개한 MNLI 무작위 부분집합' has no antecedent.
L75 restates L44's subtract-BA/add-B'A' example, so the closing section repeats the method section instead of building on it.
D: Good: L24 explains how to read the heatmap (rows, cells); L38 justifies the alpha/r scaling; L40 gives a numeric count.
L42's convergence argument (adapters -> MLP, prefix -> short-input model) is stated without a sentence of intuition for why.
E: Only one table (low-data MNLI); the paper's main comparison table (GPT-3 175B, Table 4) and the rank sweep would each be clearer as a table than the prose at L48 and L58.
The heatmap (L22) and scatter plot (L56) are placed where discussed and explained descriptively.
F: No wrong claims in the sample. Minor: L16's '약 25%' is the paper's 'speedup' figure but is attached to '처리량'; the paper's own throughput numbers give +32.6%.
U1: Motivation, method and deployment are sufficient; results lack the paper's main benchmark numbers (GPT-3 WikiSQL/MNLI/SAMSum vs FT, RoBERTa/DeBERTa GLUE, GPT-2 E2E) and the headline 10,000x / 3x reductions, so a reader cannot say how LoRA compares with full fine-tuning in numbers.
U2: TL;DR is plain prose, no math; at least one grounded limitation (L79-81). No-latency/merge point appears four times (L16, L44, L71, L75).
